target: means_of_gain (new H11 key: the ethics/method of earning, not the quantity of gains); also add 'no benefic in the 11th' to the condition, since Raman gives the mixed case its own result
quote: If maiefics be in the 11th Bhava, the native resorts to unfair and unscrupulous methods of earning, if both benefics and maiefics are there, sometimes unjust means and sometimes just methods will be resorted to. (HTJAH-II:14358-14362)
reason: The cited sentence is about HOW the native earns (unfair, unscrupulous methods). It says nothing about how much he gains, so a malefic vote on 'gains' blames the 11th for something the sentence does not say. Raman also gives a separate verdict when benefics and malefics share the 11th, so the malefic-only result should not fire when a benefic is also there. (The general line at 14351-14353, 'malefics diminish them', is a different sentence and would need its own citation.)

quote: Almost all the planets have what is called Dwirdwadasa dispositions (being in the 12th and 2nd from each other). This is an unfavourable combination which always retards success in life. ... The horoscope is that of an ordinary man, drawing about Rs. 50 to 60 a month. (HTJAH-I:2802-2805); cf. Chart 44: 'Mark the Dwirdwadasa positions ... checkered career and sudden rise and sudden fall' (HTJAH-I:2842-2843)
reason: Raman uses this dictum himself as the deciding judgment on finances in two worked second-house charts, so a malefic vote on H2 wealth with this polarity is faithful. Two housekeeping fixes: the citation should move from 2800 (the Jupiter line) to 2802-2803. And Raman's threshold is 'almost all' planets, so an 'all planets' predicate fires on fewer charts than the text covers, which errs on the safe side; check the helper's threshold.

quote: If the fifth house has beneficial associations or aspects, there will be children. (HTJAH-I:5183)
reason: The condition (a benefic in the 5th, or a benefic aspecting the 5th) is the sentence's own 'associations or aspects', and the conclusion is the presence of children, so 'children' with benefic polarity matches. The caution at 5179-5181 ('general in character requiring the skill ... of the astrologer') covers the whole list of combinations. It is not a qualification of this one, so it does not make the rule descriptive.

target: enemies (H6 key; a new 'litigation' key would also serve). The matter Raman illustrates is a legal attack by an adversary, not the native's body or self
quote: There should be no contact between lords of the 1st and 6th either by way of aspect or association. Here lord of Lagna is aspected by Mars lord of the 6th and 11th. The native was once implicated in a defamation case but subsequently acquitted. (HTJAH-I:1972-1974)
reason: The condition is faithful: lords of 1 and 6 in aspect or association, with dual lordship excluded. But the only consequence Raman ties to it is a defamation case, which is litigation and enmity, a 6th-house matter. A malefic vote on H1 'self' assigns a verdict about body or personality that the passage never draws. Note too that his illustration ends in acquittal, so the affliction is real but limited.

quote: If the lord of the 12th be in the 2nd or vice versa, the subject loses wealth under penalty. (HTJAH-I:2472)
reason: Or(12th lord in 2nd, 2nd lord in 12th) is exactly 'or vice versa'. The conclusion is loss of wealth, so H2 wealth with malefic polarity matches. No Lagna lets one planet rule both the 2nd and the 12th, so no degenerate case arises.

quote: If the 7th Bhava reckoned from the Lagna or the Moon be occupied or aspected by the 9th lord, or sign-lord or other benefics, marriage will be happy and the wife, a loving and fortunate woman. (HTJAH-II:353-356)
reason: 'Benefic occupying the 7th from Lagna' is one branch of Raman's disjunction, so every chart it fires on is covered by the sentence, and 'marriage will be happy' maps to marital_happiness with benefic polarity. The rule fires on fewer charts than the text: it leaves out aspect, the 7th from the Moon, and the 9th lord / sign-lord. That is a faithful subset, not an over-fire. The 'fortified' text claims '(from Lagna or Moon)', which the condition does not implement, so the text should be corrected or the condition broadened.

target: (Mars or the 3rd lord exalted in the RASI) OR (Mars or the 3rd lord in own sign in the rasi) OR (Mars or the 3rd lord in its own Navamsha) OR (Mars or the 3rd lord in a Navamsha owned by a benefic). Drop the D9-EXALTATION arm.
quote: Increase in brothers may be expected if the third lord or Mars occupies exaltation, his own house or Navamsha, or the Navamsha of benefices. (HTJAH-I:3432-3433)
reason: Raman names exaltation, own house, own Navamsha and a benefic's Navamsha. 'Navamsha' attaches to 'own', not to 'exaltation'. _KarakaOrLordVargaDignity also accepts D9 'exalt', which the sentence does not state. That arm adds real charts: Mars exalted in navamsa sits in Capricorn, a Saturn sign that no other arm catches. House, signification (siblings) and polarity are correct.

target: Two or more functional malefics (per-Lagna nature) occupying the Lagna, matching the 'many evil planets' threshold of the cited line and the two-planet configuration of Chart 20 (Sun and Mercury)
quote: If there are many evil planets in Lagna the person will always be miserable. (HTJAH-I:1131); Chart 20: 'The Lagna is occupied by the Sun and Mercury lords of the 2nd and 3rd. This is not very propitious ... The Sun and Mercury are malefic and their situation in Lagna is not desirable.' (HTJAH-I:2003-2004, 2010)
reason: The cited dictum needs MANY evil planets in the Lagna. The rule fires on any single functional malefic there, which covers far more charts than either the dictum or the worked case supports. Chart 20, its only other support, has two functional malefics, and Raman weighs them as one adverse factor among several. A single functional malefic in Lagna is never given a verdict anywhere in the cited text.

quote: One of the most misunderstood and misapplied astrological dicta is the one relating to the so-called evil of Mars (Kuja Dosha). (HTJAH-II:2579-2581) ... The Dosha is not absolute. (HTJAH-II:2605) ... if the dosha units in both charts are equal or nearly so, the matching can be said to be good. (HTJAH-II:2627-2628)
reason: Raman introduces the dictum as 'misunderstood and misapplied' and puts it in quotation marks as someone else's saying. He then says the dosha is not absolute, must be judged by Bhavas rather than Rasis (the rule uses rasis), and is graded in units to be weighed against the PARTNER's chart in matching. He never applies it as a single-chart verdict on marital happiness, and its literal result (death of the spouse) is not this signification either. It should be shown as text, not vote.

target: (9th lord debilitated in sign [or Navamsa]) OR (a malefic occupies the 9th AND that malefic is NOT exalted, in its own sign, or in a friendly sign)
quote: If the 9th lord be in a malefic shashtyamsa or occupy a debilitated sign or Navamsa or be weak or if malefics occupy the 9th house, the native is unfortunate in life. (HTJAH-II:7463-7465) ... But if the malefic in the 9th be exalted, in own or a friendly sign, the opposite results are produced. (HTJAH-II:7469-7470)
reason: Raman joins these clauses with 'or', so the text is a plain disjunction. The code comment reads it as a 'three-part conjunction of severity', and that reading is not in the text. The lord-debility arm is a faithful subset. But Raman immediately reverses the malefic-in-9th result when that malefic is exalted or in its own or a friendly sign, and the current malefic arm ignores that, so it fires afflicted where Raman says the opposite.

target: A malefic, combust ('eclipsed') or debilitated planet occupies the 9th, EXCEPT that a malefic in the 9th that is exalted, in its own sign or in a friendly sign does NOT fire (Raman says it gives the opposite result)
quote: If a malefic, eclipsed or debilitated planet occupy the 9th house, the native will be luckless, poor or unprincipled. But if the malefic in the 9th be exalted, in own or a friendly sign, the opposite results are produced. (HTJAH-II:7467-7470)
reason: House, polarity and signification (luckless, so fortune) match, but the sentence's own exception is left out. Raman states in the very next clause that a dignified malefic in the 9th reverses the result. So the condition must exclude malefics in exaltation, own sign or friendly sign. If not, it votes afflicted on charts Raman explicitly calls fortunate.
